chunks: O you who believe, obey God and the Prophet and those in authority among you; and if you are at variance over something, refer it to God and the Messenger, if you believe in God and the Last Day. This is good for you and the best of settlement.
ai.seo_question: Who are 'those in authority' (Ulil Amr) in Islam and how should disputes be resolved?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Ahl al-Amr' (those in authority) is specifically interpreted as the Imams, beginning with Imam Ali and the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing their divine right to leadership. The verse mandates a hierarchical obedience structure where disputes are resolved by returning to the Quran and the Sunnah of the Prophet, with the Imams serving as the authoritative interpreters of these sources. This linkage underscores that true faith is incomplete without adherence to the divinely appointed guides.
